summary.headline: Q2 FY27 total income rose 68% YoY to INR148.7 crore with EBITDA margin of 29.5%, driven by Indonesia transfer case ramp-up.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was INR148.7 crore, up 68% YoY and 5% QoQ, with EBITDA of about INR44 crore (up 99%) and PAT of about INR26 crore (up 146%). Transfer case revenue of INR80.4 crore (up 88%) led growth, helped by the Indonesia pickup program and domestic 4x4 demand. EV transmission recovered to INR11.4 crore in Q2 from a softer Q1, and components reached INR35.9 crore with exports above INR23 crore. Management reiterated an FY27 revenue target of well over INR500 crore and said H2 would be a mirror image of H1, with the Indonesia pickup program ramping down.

financial_highlights.value: INR41.6 crore; bank balances INR255.7 crore

segments.name: Transfer case
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR80.4 crore (vs INR42.7 crore, +88% YoY; +6% QoQ from INR76 crore). H1 revenue INR156.4 crore, up 91% YoY, driven by Indonesia pickup, domestic 4x4 demand and upgraded OEM launches.

segments.name: E-gear drive / EV transmission
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR11.4 crore (vs INR6.1-6.2 crore, +87% YoY), a strong sequential recovery from a soft Q1. H1 revenue INR70.2 crore (+30% YoY) per the CFO; the CEO cited INR17.2 crore for H1 EV transmission against INR13.2 crore last year.

segments.name: Components (incl. exports)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR34.6-35.9 crore (vs INR27.7-29.1 crore, +25% YoY); exports exceeded INR23 crore in the quarter, per the CEO. H1 components revenue INR67.6 crore, up 45% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of well over INR500 crore; management corrected an earlier figure and said H2 will be a mirror image of H1.
Baseline growth target of 15-20% CAGR over three to five years, with Indonesia treated as an additional surge.
Long-term aspirations of about INR1,000 crore by FY30 and INR2,000 crore beyond FY32-33; described as targets, not assured outcomes.
EBITDA to stay above 20% and ROIC target of 15-18% per quotation policy; management said ROIC has slipped since IPO due to investment.
Automatic transmission launch possibly late FY28 or very early FY29 in small numbers; an announcement is expected in December or early next year.
Sigma EV transmission series production expected in H2 FY27, with testing expected to conclude around mid-December and the Nexon and Curvv schedules driving volumes.
Indonesia execution: Mahindra part expected to finish by about February 2027; Tata part to spill over to about June 2027.
capex_capacity: Indonesia transfer case supply running at about 3,000 units a month; about 24,000 units supplied to Mahindra and about 13,000 to Tata since Q4 FY26 (per management).

US wholly owned subsidiary set up in Greenville, South Carolina, with an office at Clemson University's automotive research centre; no large US manufacturing commitment yet, but a plan exists if a quoted contract (Ford/Chrysler/Toyota Tier 1 business) is won, with a decision expected in 1-1.5 months.

Management said any future manufacturing investment will be assessed against customer commitments, program economics and tariff/logistics factors; cash is earmarked for product development and capital investment toward the INR1,000 crore goal.
Automatic transmission: quotes submitted; targeting a small-car dual-clutch solution and a rear-wheel-drive 6/8-speed for high-torque SUVs.
Manual transmission (5-speed for commercial truck) and synchronizer proposals submitted; AWD and PTU work underway with another Indian OEM.
demand_pricing: Indonesia pickup program is a surge on top of the baseline; management said Mahindra's launches have historically exceeded initial forecasts, and Mahindra's new global pickup could bring Indonesia-type volumes in FY29.
Tata Motors' acquisition of Iveco was cited as a major opportunity for 4WD LCV transmissions, transfer cases and manual transmissions.
EV transmission: Sigma program is a directed buy by Tata Motors via TACO; the Punch is excluded pending a separate component contract with a Chinese Tier 1 / Indian JV.
Export components crossed INR20+ crore quarterly run rate; production approvals received for export parts.

Management said overseas price realisation is better than India and cited European supplier distress as a source of new programs; two Japanese and two European OEM programs at prototype stage, one expected in low-volume production in H2 FY28.
Prototype order received for an EV transmission from an Indian-China JV; management stressed this is not a production award.

qa_highlights.question: Given the INR500 crore FY27 target and H1 revenue near INR290 crore, does the target look too low, and when could automatic transmission be commercialised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target should read well over INR500 crore and H2 will mirror H1. Automatic transmission launch could move up to late FY28 or very early FY29 in small volumes, with an announcement expected in December or early 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins stay around 25% into FY28 once Indonesia volumes fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a policy of EBITDA above 20% and ROIC of 15-18% in quotations. New products like automatics may start at lower margins and improve over about three years.

qa_highlights.question: How many EV programs is the company on, and when will Sigma volumes start?
qa_highlights.answer: Coverage will span all Tata vehicles except the Punch once Sigma launches. Vehicle testing at Tata is backlogged, and the test is expected to finish around mid-December, with the Sigma sole-supplier position for the gearbox from about Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 4WD run-rate of INR50 crore per quarter reasonable, and is a INR180-190 crore component business achievable in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20% baseline growth can be inferred but is hard to quantify given Mahindra's launch dynamics; FY29 could see Indonesia-type volumes. On components, INR180-190 crore in FY28 was described as not inconceivable.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Indonesia order is executed and what spills into FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahindra is about 50% shipped and expected to finish by about February 2027; Tata is below 50% and spills to about June 2027. About 24,000 units supplied to Mahindra and 13,000 to Tata.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan for cash, and is a special dividend planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cash will fund product development and capex toward the INR1,000 crore goal, in line with the IPO prospectus. No special dividend is planned.

risks_watch: Indonesia program revenue runs down in H2 and into FY28; the Tata part spills to about June 2027, so the INR500 crore FY27 target depends on H2 execution.
Sigma EV start depends on Tata's vehicle testing backlog clearing around mid-December; the timeline has already moved several times.
Automatic transmission commercialisation depends on winning a strategic OEM award; management expects an update by December or early 2027.
Cost pressures (power, commodities) against the stated margin floor of 20% EBITDA; ROIC has slipped since IPO.
US manufacturing decision: a go/no-go on a quoted contract is expected in about 1-1.5 months, with capex to follow quickly if won.
Concentration on Tata and Mahindra for both EV and transfer case revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's numbers and the Indonesia ramp, but cautious and hedged on forward targets, which management repeatedly called aspirations rather than outcomes. Evasive on specific volume and timing questions (4WD run rate, Sigma volumes, automatic launch), citing confidentiality and dynamic customer schedules.
key_quotes: So you're absolutely right. And the second half will be kind of a mirror image of the first half.
These are targets and aspirations, not assured outcomes.
The prototype order is a very important technical engagement wherein a customer recognizes our product capabilities, but it should not be interpreted at this stage as a production award.
The existence of a market opportunity alone is not a sufficient reason for major capital expenditure.

adds.what: Indonesia transfer case supply line running at about 3,000 units a month (already running, not new capacity)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to well over INR500 crore (corrected from earlier figure), with H2 described as a mirror image of H1 and Indonesia pickup ramping down; backed by Indonesia supply of ~3,000 units/month and Mahindra/Tata programme timelines, but no new capacity addition quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin was 29.5% and H1 29.4-29.5%, but management only commits to a floor above 20% and says new products like automatics start at lower margins and improve over about three years, so margins are more likely to ease than expand as Indonesia volumes fall.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Indonesia supply already runs at about 3,000 units a month (existing line, not new capacity), and no large manufacturing commitment is made; any US plant depends on winning a quoted Tier 1 contract, with a decision in 1-1.5 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to well over INR500 crore against H1 of about INR290.5 crore, which implies H2 roughly matches H1; Sigma EV series production is expected in H2 FY27, but Indonesia volumes ramp down as Mahindra finishes around Feb 2027 and Tata around June 2027.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, and management says future manufacturing investment depends on customer commitments; cash of INR255.7 crore in bank balances is earmarked for product development and capex toward the INR1,000 crore goal, so a capex decision could follow a US contract win.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management corrected the FY27 target to well over INR500 crore against H1 revenue of INR290.5 crore, which reads as conservative, but H2 is guided as a mirror image of H1 with Indonesia ramping down.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Indonesia revenue runs down in H2 and the Tata part spills to about June 2027, and Sigma timing has moved several times on Tata's testing backlog, which threatens the INR500 crore target if EV or new programmes slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sigma EV transmission series production is expected in H2 FY27 (testing to conclude around mid-December), and automatic transmission may launch in small numbers in late FY28 or very early FY29, with an announcement due in December or early 2027.

rows.label: US manufacturing decision on Tier 1 quote
rows.why: A go/no-go on a quoted Ford/Chrysler/Toyota Tier 1 contract is expected in about 1-1.5 months, and capex would follow quickly if won, though management says no large US manufacturing commitment exists yet.

rows.label: Export components and European/Japanese OEM programmes
rows.why: Exports exceeded INR23 crore in Q2 (run rate above INR20 crore a quarter), and one of four Japanese/European OEM programmes at prototype stage is expected in low-volume production in H2 FY28.

rows.label: ROIC recovery toward 15-18% target
rows.why: Management said ROIC has slipped since IPO due to investment, and no timeline for recovery was given, so returns are likely to stay depressed while capex and product development continue.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q2 numbers, the Indonesia ramp and export programmes, but cautious and hedged on forward targets, calling them aspirations rather than outcomes; analysts pressed on whether the INR500 crore FY27 target is too low, on the FY28 4WD run rate and components of INR180-190 cror
